title: Stream consolidator: latency equalizer with kernel probing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a lightweight 'stream consolidator' admission layer that smooths bursty prefill traffic, normalizes tail latency across heterogeneous kernels, and surfaces kernel-probing hints for attention prefetching. The goal is to reduce 99th/99.9th percentile prefill+decode latency variance without regressing median latency or throughput.

Problem: We observe disproportionate tail latency when short, high-priority prefill requests interleave with long-context requests that trigger different kernel paths. The current admission logic admits raw arrival order which causes kernel thrashing, KV cache churn, and decode stalls for in-flight streams. Existing batch shapers reduce average cost but do not actively redistribute admission headroom to limit tails.

Goals:
- Reduce 99th/99.9th prefill+decode latency by 20-35% for mixed workloads.
- Maintain median latency within +/-5% of baseline.
- Avoid lowering overall throughput for dedicated pools.
- Provide observability hooks (per-kernel quantiles, admission decisions, token pacing) for fast debugging and rollbacks.

Non-goals:
- Global model-level admission redesign; this ticket is focused on a runtime admission shim and local kernel-aware heuristics.
- Rewriting kernel implementations themselves.

Design (high level):
1) Rolling-quantile admission budget: maintain per-queue EWMA of observed decode latencies (p50/p95/p99) and compute a rolling admission budget that reserves a small fraction of slots for infrequent short requests to avoid starvation. Budget is expressed in token-equivalent units so heterogeneous sequence lengths are comparable.

2) Kernel-probing score: compute a lightweight kernel affinity score for incoming requests using model metadata (quantized vs fp16), sequence-length histogram, and a short sampled microbenchmark (fast probe executed at low sampling rate). The score is a 0..1 hint used by the admission shim to prioritize co-locating requests with matching expected kernel paths.

3) Attention-prefetch hinting: when a request's kernel score indicates an attention-optimized kernel, attach a prefetch hint that triggers KV cache prewarm for compatible concurrent streams on the same GPU node. Prefetch is bounded and backpressure-aware to avoid adding token overhead.

4) Staggered decode windows: for long sequences that would trigger a costly kernel switch mid-decode, the consolidator will slightly stagger admission times (sub-ms to tens-of-ms depending on latency SLO) to align kernel usage and reduce mid-decode kernel swapping. The stagger amount is dynamic based on load and tail risk.

5) Microburst detector and temporary reservation: detect sudden spikes (microbursts) and temporarily reserve a small set of admission slots for high-priority short requests to prevent them from being queued behind large prefill waves.

Instrumentation and metrics:
- per-kernel p50/p95/p99 for prefill and decode phases
- admission decision reason tag (budget, kernel_affinity, microburst_reserve, overflow)
- token-equivalent admission budget utilization over time
- KV-prefetch hit/miss rate and prefetch overhead in tokens
- counts of staggered admits and mean stagger delay

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): implement read-only metric plumbing + shadow admission decisions for 2 weeks on a subset of hosts (metric-only to validate policy signals).
- Stage 2 (controlled): enable admission decisions with kernel-probing score at 5% traffic for a single model family, monitor 99/99.9 tail and throughput for 3 days. Auto-rollback threshold: 99th tail > baseline by 10% or throughput drop > 5%.
- Stage 3 (broader): widen to 25% and tune parameters (reserve size, EWMA half-life, sampling rate).
- Stage 4: default enable with opt-out per-tenant policy and A/B testing for edge cases.

Experimentation plan:
- Synthetic mixed workload (short bursty + long-context): baseline vs consolidator ON.
- Real customer trace replay for 3 top tenants to validate behavior.
- Ablation tests: kernel score off, prefetch off, stagger off to isolate impact.

Acceptance criteria:
- Measured 99th latency reduction >=20% on synthetic mix and >=15% on replays.
- Median latency within +/-5% of baseline.
- No KV-prefetch token overhead >1% of overall token usage in canary.
- Metric coverage for all instrumentation is shipping to Grafana and dashboards created.

Risks and mitigations:
- Over-eager prefetch increases token cost: bound prefetch budget, measure and roll back if >1% overhead.
- Staggering adds latency to some requests: tune stagger horizon and only apply when tail risk high.
- Kernel affinity misclassification: low sampling probe and fallback to conservative admission.

Deliverables:
- runtime: lightweight consolidator admission module (C++/Rust code + config knobs)
- telemetry: metrics + Grafana dashboard
- load-tests: synthetic harness and trace replayer scripts
- docs: runbook and rollout instructions

Notes: this ticket intentionally focuses on admission + hints; kernel implementation improvements and full kernel auto-scheduler will be separate follow-ups.
